entities.summary:
Jean Parmentier (1494–1529), born in Dieppe, France, was a navigator, cartographer, and poet. He made numerous voyages for the shipowner Jean Ango, mapping the coastlines of France, Britain, and Ireland. His brother Raoul accompanied him on many of these expeditions. Jean Parmentier's navigational skills and knowledge of the British Isles helped establish France's maritime claims in the region. 

The voyages of Jean Parmentier and his brother Raoul were crucial in the development of French navigation and cartography. Their journeys not only mapped the coastlines of France, Britain, and Ireland but also helped to establish trade routes and identify potential resources. These expeditions played a significant role in the emergence of France as a major maritime power in the 16th century. 

Jean Parmentier's legacy extends beyond his navigational skills and cartographic achievements. He was also a poet and played a significant role in the cultural life of Dieppe. His poetry reflects the beauty of the French coastlines and the people who lived there. 

One of the most striking aspects of Jean Parmentier's life is his navigation of the British Isles. In 1528, he sailed to the coast of Wales, mapping the coastline and identifying potential resources. This journey marked a significant turning point in the development of French navigation and cartography. 

The impact of Jean Parmentier's voyages can still be seen today. His maps of the British Isles and France continue to be studied by historians and cartographers. His navigational skills and knowledge of the region helped establish France's maritime claims, paving the way for future explorers and traders.
